paragraphs: So he is cited in Seder HaDorot from Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:2. It also reports that this is the reading in Sedeh Yehoshua. But Hyman does not find this name in our Jerusalem Talmud.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The absence of the name from “our Jerusalem Talmud” is Hyman’s observation, not a fresh search of all versions.

The consulted Seder HaDorot notice names Yishmael ben Gamliel, suggests that Shimon should perhaps be read, and reports that Sedeh Yehoshua also reads Yishmael. The checked Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot passage has bracketed Shimon in the consulted digital edition. Sedeh Yehoshua and the other version suggested by search results were not independently collated. Hyman’s statement about his Jerusalem Talmud remains his own observation, without a claim about every version.
